cloudTrail.recommendedUsing: Use CloudTrail to audit configurations, detect unauthorized API calls, trace security incidents, and ensure compliance reporting.
cloudTrail.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid turning off CloudTrail in any production account, as it is the fundamental baseline for security compliance, forensics, and auditing.
cloudTrail.practicalScenario: An administrator uses CloudTrail to find out who deleted a production database, identifying the exact IAM user and time of the API call.
keyCharacteristics: Records all AWS API calls, user logins, and CLI operations.
Saves log trails to S3 with cryptographic validation checks.
Integrates with EventBridge to trigger alarms on specific API actions.
Provides multi-region and multi-account auditing trails.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Deliver audit log trails to secure Amazon S3 buckets.
Stream trail events to CloudWatch Logs for real-time analysis.
Analyze historical trail logs using Amazon Athena queries.
Delivers trail events to CloudWatch Logs and surfaces API events on EventBridge.

backup.overview: AWS Backup is a fully managed backup service that makes it easy to centralize and automate the backup of data across AWS services.
backup.conceptualModel: Think of AWS Backup as a scheduled vault system that takes periodic snapshots of your office documents, database drives, and servers, storing them safely.
backup.recommendedUsing: Use AWS Backup to enforce backup schedule policies, manage backup retention, encrypt snapshots, and coordinate compliance recovery points.
backup.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid manual snapshot management scripts for individual databases; use AWS Backup to centralize and automate snapshot lifecycles.
backup.practicalScenario: A company configures AWS Backup to take daily snapshots of all RDS databases, retaining the backups for 30 days automatically.
keyCharacteristics: Centralizes backup policies across multiple AWS services.
Automates backup schedules, retention, and lifecycle transitions.
Supports cross-region and cross-account backup copies.
Ensures regulatory compliance with write-once-read-many (WORM) vaults.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Backup database storage volumes on Amazon RDS and Aurora.
Take snapshots of EBS server drives and S3 Buckets.
Log backup task events and status updates to CloudWatch.
Recovery points are stored in S3-backed backup vaults.

appRunner.overview: AWS AppRunner is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to quickly deploy containerized web applications and APIs at scale.
appRunner.conceptualModel: Think of AppRunner as a streamlined express lane. You give it your source code or Docker image, and it handles load balancers, domain names, scaling, and runtime.
appRunner.recommendedUsing: Use AppRunner for simple REST APIs, web apps, backend microservices, and fast prototype deployments without managing VPC network plumbing.
appRunner.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid AppRunner for complex, multi-container architectures that require custom network overlays, mesh control, or Kubernetes configurations (use EKS instead).
appRunner.practicalScenario: A developer connects AppRunner to their GitHub repo. Every time they commit code, AppRunner rebuilds the container and deploys it behind an SSL balancer.
keyCharacteristics: Fully managed—abstracts load balancers, ECS cluster hosts, and SSL.
Integrates directly with GitHub repositories or ECR images.
Scales application container count automatically to match traffic.
Provides private VPC endpoint routing configurations.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Deploy container images published to Elastic Container Registry (ECR).
Secure backend connection strings using Secrets Manager.
Route domains using Route 53 DNS records.
Containers reach S3, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, and Secrets Manager.

elasticBeanstalk.overview: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is an easy-to-use service for deploying and scaling web applications and services developed with Java, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, and Go.
elasticBeanstalk.conceptualModel: Think of Elastic Beanstalk as a managed server template. You upload your application code zip, and it automatically sets up EC2 instances, load balancers, and Auto Scaling.
elasticBeanstalk.recommendedUsing: Use Elastic Beanstalk when you want to deploy standard web applications quickly while retaining full access and control over the underlying EC2 servers.
elasticBeanstalk.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid Beanstalk for modern cloud-native systems where container-first pipelines (like AppRunner, ECS, or Lambda) are more efficient and require less management.
elasticBeanstalk.practicalScenario: A team deploys a Node.js web app to Elastic Beanstalk, which automatically provisions an ALB, EC2 instances, and configures security groups.
keyCharacteristics: Deploys web applications from simple source code zip uploads.
Provisions standard architectures (EC2, Load Balancers, Auto Scaling).
Retains full root control over the generated AWS resources.
Supports platform updates for OS and runtime environments.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Host web interfaces fronted by Application Load Balancers.
Connect database backends on Amazon RDS.
Store uploaded static files inside Amazon S3.
EB applications call S3, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, CloudWatch, and Secrets Manager via SDK.

fsx.overview: Amazon FSx provides fully managed, high-performance file systems, making it easy to launch and scale popular file systems (Lustre, Windows File Server, OpenZFS).
fsx.conceptualModel: Think of FSx as a high-performance network drive designed for speed. It allows specialized enterprise applications to access files at sub-millisecond speeds.
fsx.recommendedUsing: Use FSx for high-performance computing (HPC) jobs, Windows-based shared drives, video rendering pipelines, and database storage migrations.
fsx.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid FSx for simple shared storage workloads where standard Elastic File System (EFS) or S3 object storage is more cost-effective.
fsx.practicalScenario: A financial model simulation cluster of 50 servers mounts an FSx for Lustre file system to read and process raw transaction datasets at 100 GB/s.
keyCharacteristics: Provides managed Windows File Server, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP, and OpenZFS.
Delivers sub-millisecond latencies and high throughput.
Supports shared access for Windows and Linux applications.
Enables serverless file storage scaling automatically.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Provide shared network storage for Windows EC2 instances.
Integrate FSx for Lustre with Amazon S3 data lakes for HPC jobs.
Mount high-performance volumes on container tasks in ECS/EKS.
FSx for Lustre tiers data with S3; all file systems can be backed up by AWS Backup.

certificateManager.overview: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) makes it easy to provision, manage, and deploy public and private Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS) certificates.
certificateManager.conceptualModel: Think of ACM as your digital notary. It issues security certificates, stamps them, and automatically renews them so your website connection remains encrypted (HTTPS).
certificateManager.recommendedUsing: Always use ACM to manage SSL/TLS certificates for public websites, secure REST APIs, and encrypt connections at load balancers and CDNs.
certificateManager.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid using ACM to install certificates on standalone EC2 instances; ACM is designed to bind directly to managed AWS resources like ALBs and CloudFront.
certificateManager.practicalScenario: ACM issues a wild-card certificate for '*.mycompany.com' and attaches it to an ALB, enabling HTTPS traffic encryption for all web subdomains.
keyCharacteristics: Provisions public and private SSL/TLS certificates.
Handles automatic renewal of certificates before they expire.
Provides free public certificates when used with AWS resources.
Integrates natively with CloudFront, ALB, and API Gateway.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Bind SSL certificates to Application Load Balancers.
Secure global edge CDN distributions on CloudFront.
Encrypt public APIs hosted on Amazon API Gateway.

systemsManager.overview: AWS Systems Manager is a management service that helps you collect operational data, automate tasks, and manage resources across AWS and on-premises environments.
systemsManager.conceptualModel: Think of Systems Manager as a remote control and diagnostic tool for all your servers. You can run scripts, check patches, and login without needing direct keys.
systemsManager.recommendedUsing: Use Systems Manager to store application configurations (Parameter Store), execute remote commands on EC2 instances, apply software updates, and secure shell logins.
systemsManager.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid opening SSH (port 22) or RDP to the public internet; use Systems Manager Session Manager for secure, keyless command-line access.
systemsManager.practicalScenario: An operator uses Systems Manager Parameter Store to fetch a database URL, and uses Session Manager to log into a private EC2 server without exposing SSH ports.
keyCharacteristics: Provides Session Manager for secure shell access without SSH keys.
Provides Parameter Store for centralized config and secret management.
Automates OS patching and server software configurations.
Aggregates operational dashboards across AWS resources.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Retrieve application settings from Parameter Store.
Manage configurations on EC2 virtual servers.
Log admin session histories securely to CloudWatch Logs.
Run Command and Patch Manager target EC2, ECS, and EKS hosts via the SSM Agent.
Publishes automation execution metrics and logs to CloudWatch.

ecr.overview: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is a fully managed container registry that makes it easy for developers to share and deploy container images.
ecr.conceptualModel: Think of ECR as a library catalog of container blueprints (Docker images). Developers deposit images there, and the container hosts pull them out to launch containers.
ecr.recommendedUsing: Use ECR to store, manage, and scan Docker images that will be deployed to container services like ECS, EKS, or AppRunner.
ecr.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid ECR for generic file storage or backups; use S3 for standard objects and files and keep ECR dedicated to container images.
ecr.practicalScenario: A CodeBuild step compiles a microservice into a Docker image and pushes it to ECR. An ECS service pulls the image from ECR to deploy the update.
keyCharacteristics: Fully managed Docker container registry service.
Performs automatic security scans for container vulnerabilities.
Secures container images using IAM policies and encryption.
Supports public and private container registries.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Retrieve images to launch container tasks in ECS.
Pull deployment pod blueprints in EKS clusters.
Upload Docker images compiled by AWS CodeBuild.
Distributes container images to EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda, and App Runner.

privateLink.overview: AWS PrivateLink establishes secure, private connectivity between VPCs, AWS services, and on-premises networks without exposing traffic to the public internet.
privateLink.conceptualModel: Think of PrivateLink as laying a private, insulated tube between two buildings. Traffic moves directly through the tube, completely bypassing the public street (internet).
privateLink.recommendedUsing: Use PrivateLink to connect your VPC to AWS services (like S3 or DynamoDB) or third-party APIs privately, keeping all traffic within the AWS backbone network.
privateLink.recommendedAvoiding: Avoid PrivateLink for basic public internet connections, as it is designed for private endpoint routing and security compliance.
privateLink.practicalScenario: A backend container in a private subnet query database API logs on RDS via a PrivateLink endpoint, ensuring no data packets exit the VPC boundary.
keyCharacteristics: Keeps service-to-service traffic inside the AWS private network.
Creates private endpoint IP addresses (VPC Endpoints) inside subnets.
Prevents data exposure to the public internet.
Simplifies networking by eliminating NAT Gateways and route configs.
commonIntegrationPatterns: Connect private VPC resources securely to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB.
Expose APIs hosted on internal load balancers to client VPCs.
Interface private subnets with AWS Secrets Manager.
